result.title: VSpark: Speculative Decoding for Autoregressive Vision-Language-Action Models
result.summary: Our aim is to accelerate autoregressive vision-language-action models (VLAs), which generate robot actions one token at a time. Speculative decoding makes this possible: a lightweight draft model proposes several tokens at once, and the VLA verifies them in a single pass, accepting only those that match its own predictions, so decoding remains lossless. The speedup, however, is limited in robot control, where many different tokens encode nearly the same motion and a draft close to the correct action is still rejected. To address this, our approach, VSpark, is built upon three design choices: (i) rollouts collected with calibrated action noise, which expose the draft to a wider range of robot states; (ii) feature alignment, which trains the draft to match the VLA's hidden features rather than its output tokens alone; and (iii) continuation reuse, which keeps the predictions the VLA has already computed along rejected drafts as candidates for the next verification step, instead of discarding them. On four VLAs with different action tokenizers and four manipulation benchmarks, VSpark achieves 1.28x to 2.10x speedup while keeping the VLA's decoding lossless.

AI.brief_summary: VSpark 针对逐 token 生成机器人动作的自回归 VLA，采用轻量草稿模型提议、VLA 单次验证的投机解码，并结合动作噪声 rollout、隐藏特征对齐和被拒草稿续用来加速且保持无损。
AI.relevance_reason: 其草稿—验证、隐藏特征对齐与拒绝候选复用可能为 latent 推理状态的并行提议、验证及回退更新提供方法线索，但面向机器人动作解码，能否迁移到多模态推理尚待核查。
